answer: A registration fee is just a speed bump; a Sybil attacker pays it many times. The real mechanism is a per-identity bond that staked graders slash after a verified bad vote or copied answer. Sybil swarms must vote in lockstep, so one slashing drains every fake identity at once, and collusion shows as a sharp signal on a single ridge of correlated accounts. To stay hidden the attacker parks real capital idle across all fakes for many epochs. Yarrow-style sharding keeps that capital bar steady per identity instead of thinning as the pool grows, so break-even cost scales with the voices needed.
